releases.notes:
- **Auto-install (optional, off by default):** turn it on with the **Auto-install** chip on the updates screen, the OneConfig page, or `autoInstall` in the config. Updates it's sure about then go in without asking: full releases on Modrinth for your loader and Minecraft version, or GitHub files named for your Minecraft version, always with a published hash. Betas, alphas and anything less certain are still left for you.
  - With a pre-launch check (Prism or OneClient), they're installed before the game starts and the window lists only the rest (or closes by itself).
  - On any other launcher, they're downloaded as the game starts and swapped in when it closes, ready for the next launch.

releases.notes:
- **Fixed OneClient:** OneClient runs most clusters in one shared game folder, so the mod was looking in the wrong mods folder ("0 mods checked") and never offered the pre-launch **Set up**. It now uses the cluster's real mods folder, and the pre-launch check works out which cluster is starting and does nothing for clusters without this mod.
- **Bundled mods are checked again:** mods from OneClient's bundles are updated like the rest and labelled *OneClient bundle*. OneClient keeps the new jar and switches the bundle's copy off, so its bundle updates don't bring the old one back.
- **No more wrong-version GitHub updates:** when a repo's latest release is for another Minecraft version (like `2.4.0+26.3`), the newest release for yours is used instead, or none.

releases.notes:
- **Pre-launch check in OneClient:** when OneClient starts the game, the updates screen (and the OneConfig page) offers **Set up**. When you close the game, OneClient closes, its Pre-Launch Command is set (with a backup; an existing command is never replaced) and it reopens. It only runs in clusters that have this mod. OneClient starts the game even if the command fails, so the window has no Quit button there.
- **Choose what the pre-launch check does:** the new **Before launch** setting (`prelaunchMode`: update window, install all, log only, or off) is on the OneConfig page, in `config/modupdatechecker.json`, and as a chip on the updates screen once a pre-launch check is set up. It applies the next launch, with no launcher change.
- Commands that already pass `--install` or `--gui` keep working while the setting is on its default (update window). A command with neither option now opens the update window instead of only logging; set **Before launch** to *Log only* to keep the old behaviour.

releases.notes:

releases.notes:
Finds mod problems, replacing the Duplicate Mod Warning mod. Earlier versions of Mod Update Checker offer this update by themselves.

- **Duplicate mods:** several copies of one mod (same file, mod id or name) are listed, keeping the highest version. Identical copies keep the one not named like a copy (`mod (1).jar`). Copies that only share a name are flagged to check first.
- **Mods for other loaders:** Forge, NeoForge, Quilt, LiteLoader, Rift and LabyMod jars, which Ornithe never loads.
- **Duplicate Mod Warning isn't needed any more:** if it's installed, it's offered for removal.
- Fixing moves jars to `removed-mods` (next to `mods`), so nothing is deleted. A jar the game has open is moved when the game closes.
- **In game:** a **Problems** tab that opens by itself on the title screen, and the menu button turns red (**Mod Problems**).
- **Before launch:** the `--gui` window lists problems above the updates and fixes them before installing anything. `--install` moves extra copies out by itself.
- With two copies of a mod installed, the update check now checks the copy that's kept.
- New setting `checkModProblems` (default on), also on the OneConfig page.

releases.notes:
Safer installs. Mod Update Checker 1.0.0 offers this update by itself.

- **Wrong Minecraft version:** a download made for another Minecraft version (read from its `depends.minecraft`) is now refused, so a GitHub release built for e.g. 1.21 can't be installed and crash the game.
- **Wrong loader:** Modrinth updates are only looked for on the loader the installed version was made for, so an Ornithe mod is never "updated" to a Legacy Fabric build.
- **Other mods' files:** an update is refused if its file name is already taken in `mods` by a different mod, instead of overwriting that mod.
- **Pre-launch window:** it only stays open when there's something that can be installed (updates without a file go to the launcher's log), and each update now has an **Ignore** button.

releases.notes:
First release, for Minecraft 1.8.9 on Ornithe. Needs PolyCompose 3.0+ and Java 25; OneConfig 1.9+ is optional.

- Checks every mod in `mods` for updates: on Modrinth by file hash, and on GitHub releases for mods that link their repository.
- Mod Updates screen (PolyCompose) from a button on the title screen and pause menu: changelogs, open a mod's page, ignore a version, update one mod or all of them. Follows your GUI scale and, with OneConfig, its theme.
- Downloads are hash-checked and must be the same mod, then swapped in when the game closes.
- OneConfig page (Utility, or `/modupdates`) with Open, Update All and Check Again.
- Pre-launch check for Prism Launcher, with a window to pick which updates to install before the game starts (or Quit). The in-game screen can set the command up for you.
- Tells you when OneClient started the game, since OneClient updates mods itself, and offers to remove this mod.
- Updates itself from this repository's releases.

Setup for the pre-launch check is in the [README](https://github.com/ooTruffle/ModUpdateChecker#before-launch-prism-launcher).
